assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original actual gameplay screenshot concept art for a Korean folklore 2D pixel-art party RPG article, one single widescreen 16:9 game screen.
Primary request: "Night-shift Resolvers", a top-down party RPG with real-time ATB timelines and pause when a party member is ready. The important player decision is interrupt timing and delaying an upcoming hostile action. Show a paused command decision in an actual game screen.
Scene/backdrop: a charming small Korean hanok courtyard at night, surrounded by indigo tiled roofs, wooden porches, warm paper lanterns, potted plants and stone paving. A glowing round bamboo sieve placed on the ground distracts a playful little rumor spirit counting its holes.
Subject and composition: Clear orthographic TOP-DOWN gameplay camera at slight old-school RPG tilt, coherent square tiles. Exactly three visibly distinct party characters spread across the courtyard: a teal-hanbok human resolver selected by cyan ground ring, a masked performer in cream and coral hanbok with a small fan, and an ochre-clothed artisan with a toolkit. Across from them are three playful shadow/rumor spirits with friendly mischievous expressions, not horror monsters. The selected resolver aims a thin cyan targeting line toward one spirit beginning a purple windup with a circular interrupted-cast icon above it. Another spirit is bent over the glowing sieve.
Gameplay UI: At the very top a LARGE easily readable single horizontal ATB timeline running left-to-right across most of the screen. Portrait markers of the three party members and spirits are positioned along it; the upcoming spirit's portion is a conspicuous PURPLE WINDUP segment that can be interrupted. A small numeral 0 at left, 2 and 4 along the bar; tiny label "WINDUP" over the purple section is okay. Highlight the selected resolver's portrait marker with the same cyan outline as their ground ring. Toward the lower right a clearly visible parchment command panel with the short label "PAUSED", exactly three large command buttons shown as icons (small hand bell for interrupt, tied cord for delay, footprints for move). The bell button is selected with a cyan border. Lower left has exactly three compact party portraits with slim energy/health bars. UI occupies deliberate margins, playfield remains readable.
Style/medium: entirely crisp handcrafted 2D pixel art, visible square pixel clusters, game-native low-resolution sprite aesthetic, flat 2D tilemap, no smooth painting and no 3D. Coherent screen capture mockup, not key art.
Color palette: limited deep indigo, jade teal, warm ochre, parchment cream; purple only as the upcoming windup warning.
Constraints: opaque background; 16:9 widescreen. One gameplay screen only, not collage. NO CARDS and no deck UI. No large title, no logo, no watermark, no dense text, no Korean lettering required. Only tiny numerals and the short labels "PAUSED" and "WINDUP" if helpful. No gore, photorealism, blur, isometric diorama or poster composition. Clearly show timing, selected command and interrupt target.
visual_observations: Single elevated courtyard scene with three distinct party characters and three playful spirits.
Top timeline includes six portrait markers and a visible purple WINDUP segment.
Selected resolver has a cyan ring and targeting line to a winding-up spirit; another spirit bends over a glowing bamboo sieve.
PAUSED command panel shows bell, knot, and footprint icons, with the bell highlighted; no cards are present.
Camera is a diagonal elevated tile view rather than a strictly orthographic top-down production map.
